Subject: Post-call: Sentinel AI throughput & latency recap + next technical steps

Hi Ibrahim,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap of what we heard and the technical follow-ups we agreed on. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain & goals you emphasized:
- End-user latency spikes during peak shopping events (Black Friday-like bursts) causing measurable drop in conversions. Target: 99th percentile < 350 ms for single-turn text generation.
- Steady-state throughput target of ~120 requests/sec for the recommendations endpoint (average prompt ~90 tokens; 1:1 user-per-request).
- Strong data isolation requirement and auditability for model inputs (PCI-adjacent workloads).

Model & quality constraints:
- You prefer an open/hosted model stack; target baseline is an Llama2-13B-family model (fp16 or 4-bit quantized) with minimal quality regression vs current SOTA.
- Must support KV cache persistence across short sessions (up to 30 minutes) for repeated interactive requests.

Deployment topology we discussed:
- Dedicated GPU pool (DGX-like) in us-west for primary traffic, with a failover region in us-east.
- Autoscaler tuned for fast spin-up + burst capacity (scale-up within 45s target).
- Local prefix caching for common prompts + request-level batching (max batch latency budget 28ms) to meet p50/p95 targets.
- Fallback policy to a smaller quantized 7B variant during extreme bursts to preserve availability.

SLOs we captured (tentative, to be finalized in design review):
- Latency: p50 < 60 ms, p95 < 180 ms, p99 < 350 ms (generation to first token streamed).
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s, burst to 450 req/s for <10 minutes with graceful degraded quality fallback.
- Error budget/availability: 99.5% over 30-day rolling window for production route.

Attachments included (see attached diagram & perf matrix):
- sentinel_deployment_diagram_v1.png (deployment topology sketch)
- sentinel_perf_sla_matrix.xlsx (initial SLO/throughput matrix)

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Marissa: schedule architecture review with your infra team (suggest Wed 2027-08-11, 10:00 PT) — ACTION: confirm attendees.
- Karthik: produce an initial perf-sensitive topology proposal (including batching & KV cache params) by EOD Mon 2027-08-16.
- Aditya: share SOC2 evidence checklist and pricing sketch for Dedicated pool by Tue 2027-08-10.

If that looks right I can pull together a short design doc and run it by our runtime team before Wed.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Thanks — quick technical notes and assumptions from my side (will expand in the topology doc):

Assumptions:
- Average prompt ~90 tokens, model 13B quantized ~5 tokens/sec per GPU CUDA core equivalence (approx; dependent on kernel).
- Desired sustained 120 req/s implies ~4–6 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady state (with continuous batching & KV caching). Burst to 450 req/s requires autoscale to ~18 GPUs with burst buffer and async queueing for non-interactive requests.

Topology recommendations (initial):
- Primary: Dedicated GPU pool (us-west) composed of 6 active serving replicas behind a fast-path router (per-route token limit 512).
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch latency budget 25 ms; per-replica micro-batches sized by observed arrival distribution.
- KV cache: in-memory per-replica cache with optional encrypted persistence to customer KMS-backed store (we'll need to coordinate key policy for Private deployment).
- Fallback: Canary routing to 7B quantized model (cheaper replicas) once queue length > 3s average latency or CPU is saturated.
- Observability: token-level tracing + per-route p50/p95/p99 dashboards; increase sampling for 99th percentile traces during blackouts.

Open items to confirm in design review:
- Concrete KMS integration method for KV encryption (bring security engineer if needed).
- Exact traffic shaping (burst window size) and acceptable quality delta for 7B fallback.
- Contractual SLA language for burst-capacity tail events.

I'll produce the topology bullets and an estimated cost range for Dedicated capacity by EOD Mon 2027-08-16.
